correctness.rationale: For a nonadjacent pair in a 2-plex, every other member must be adjacent to both. Hamming-distance-two pairs have precisely two common neighbors and pairs of greater distance none. This restricts noncliques to a three-vertex path or a four-vertex coordinate square, and larger sets to coordinate-line cliques. The proof independently establishes which pairs, squares and full coordinate lines are inclusion-maximal, then counts all cliques and uniquely completed paths and squares without overlap. Eleven graph products of at most 18 vertices were checked exhaustively against direct membership and maximality, totaling 468037 nonempty subsets; three larger products had generated-family checks only. Computation is not the source of the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The exact line–square–distance characterization and both size polynomials for arbitrary mixed-factor Hamming graphs were compared to generic 2-plex algorithms, generic co-2-plex polynomial recurrences on graph complements, Hamming graph embeddings and related enumerations. None of the materially inspected sources states the displayed specialized classification or formulas, nor supplies a single direct graph-family specialization from which they follow without a new coordinate argument. The positive judgment is best-knowledge, not a priority guarantee. A relevant Hamming embedding article was abstract-only and the visual rendering of an older PDF was unavailable.

value.rationale: The theorem treats a standard arbitrary-dimensional family rather than an unmotivated small parameter choice, giving both complete 2-plex and complete maximal-2-plex cardinality polynomials and a natural geometric classification. The size support of maximal solutions is exactly controlled by factor sizes and Hamming diameter; homogeneous H(d,q) for d>=3 and q>=6 has an arbitrary gap of q-5 unavailable sizes. This is an exact structural enumerative fact, not a mere scalar extremal or known-table recomputation.
